clue.text: May be playing what instrument?

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so the following word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which instrument someone called May might be playing.
explanation.walkthrough: May looks like a verb or a woman's name; it is the shrub whose blossom appears in May.
explanation.definitionFit: May is the common English country name for the hawthorn shrub and its white blossom.

clue.text: Feather on cock's comb

blocks.note: first meaning: a long neck plume of a rooster
second meaning: a steel comb for dressing flax or hemp

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cock's comb' reads as the red crest on a rooster's head; the clue splits after cock's.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackles are the long shiny neck feathers of a cockerel, and a hackle is also a toothed tool for combing flax.

clue.text: Presentation of name in black, traditionally?

indicators.note: the abbreviation is put inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: how a bereaved wife traditionally dressed: in black mourning

explanation.surface: A formal announcement of someone's name, printed in black type in the traditional way.
explanation.walkthrough: Widows traditionally wore black, so 'widow dressing' is dressing in black; N slips into the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Window-dressing is a showy presentation that makes something look better than it really is, from arranging shop displays.

clue.text: One of the other messengers?

indicators.note: one of a group is a part of it, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A grumble about a courier from a rival delivery firm rather than the usual postman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the Greek gods had more than one herald, and this is the other besides Iris; a UK parcel firm also bore the name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the winged-sandalled son of Zeus served as herald of the gods alongside Iris.

clue.text: Inform about one accomplice with good reason

indicators.note: going about something means encircling it, so the informing phrase wraps the numeral

blocks.note: to rat on someone is to inform against them

explanation.surface: A justified decision to grass up a partner in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting rationally means acting sensibly and logically, on sound grounds rather than by impulse.

clue.text: Sweet to charge around loudly

indicators.note: a charge going around something wraps itself about the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: a fee is a charge for a service
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: Someone noisily charging round a sweet shop, or a sweet way to bill people.
explanation.walkthrough: The F for loudly goes inside the word for a charge, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter, one kind of sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Whine to be surrounded by former luxury

indicators.note: something surrounded is enclosed on all sides by the word that follows

explanation.surface: Complaints about having lost the high life of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth displayed through lavish, costly living, which is luxury.

clue.text: "Square"?

blocks.note: surface reading: a geometric shape with four equal sides, a kind of figure
setter's reading: the word in quotation marks, used of a dull conventional person, is a metaphorical expression

explanation.walkthrough: A square is a figure in geometry, but the quotation marks make it slang for a stuffy person, a word used figuratively.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a square is a metaphorical use of language, which is what an idiom or trope is.

clue.text: Queen's cut off without practice

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the cut wraps round the monarch

blocks.note: to excise is to remove by cutting

explanation.surface: Royalty left without training or rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here; the 's is 'is', joining the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise as a noun means drill or training, repeated activity to build skill, as does practice.

clue.text: Island psychiatrist gets student in shape for urban nightmare

indicators.note: one thing getting another means it acquires it, so the parts are joined end to end
the joined parts are placed inside the word for a shape

explanation.surface: An island-based psychiatrist takes on a student to help shape their thinking about an urban nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: The shape is split open, its last letter after everything else, so the island, psychiatrist and student all sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A concrete jungle is a harsh, crowded city landscape of buildings without greenery, a nightmare version of urban life.

clue.text: See 9
Approval to hesitate when idiot is bearing witness

indicators.note: one word added to another simply follows it
something bearing a load carries it within, so the idiot holds the other pieces

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over giving approval while a fool is testifying in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing witness' reads as one phrase, but 'bearing' belongs to the wordplay and 'witness' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker who watches events without taking part has seen them, so is a witness.

clue.text: Miss the mark in swinging clubs, if holding iron

indicators.note: a swinging object turns about, so the following two pieces are read backwards
the missed shot goes inside the turned-around pair

blocks.note: to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: A golfer swinging clubs misses the target even when using an iron.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs and iron suggest golf; clubs is the card suit and iron is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferric is the chemistry adjective for compounds containing iron, especially in its trivalent state.

clue.text: Don't resign stupidly, as this will give you an edge

definitions.text: this will give you an edge

indicators.note: acting stupidly scrambles things, so the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice not to quit foolishly, since staying put will give you the advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An edge' sounds like a competitive advantage; it is a literal sharp blade edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A grindstone is a revolving stone wheel used for sharpening tools and blades, putting a keen edge on them.

clue.text: Extensive substitution of scripture for article becomes fickle

indicators.note: a substitution swaps one thing for another, here a scripture lesson for an article

blocks.note: RI, religious instruction, the old school subject

explanation.surface: A text heavily rewritten with scripture in place of an article turns unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in CAPACIOUS is swapped out for RI; RI is religious instruction, a school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricious describes someone given to sudden unpredictable changes of mood, exactly a fickle temperament.

clue.text: Odd for an average rating?

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, a naval rating

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark that an ordinary score should be thought strange.
explanation.walkthrough: Rating looks like a score; it is a sailor, and an ordinary one would be a 'normal AB', with the pieces reversed in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means departing from what is usual or expected, which is what odd describes.

clue.text: See 2
Remark by unhappy sailor washed up on the shore?

definitions.note: a cryptic sense, SEA'S HELL, rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a miserable mariner's complaint that life at sea is torment
second meaning: the empty casing of a mollusc found on a beach

explanation.walkthrough: Split as SEA'S HELL it is the sailor's lament; read whole it is something found on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Shells of molluscs are cast up by the tide and collected by beachcombers along the tideline.

clue.text: Disputed frontier

blocks.note: first meaning: doubtful, open to argument
second meaning: a line marking a border

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about contested borders; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A borderline case is uncertain and arguable, while a border line literally divides two territories.

clue.text: Secured for take off in the past

blocks.note: first meaning: fastened with a sliding bar
second meaning: ran away suddenly, past tense

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a plane fastened down ready for take-off; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolted door is fastened shut, and a horse that bolted dashed off in panic.

clue.text: See 7
Get nowhere in court after Waterloo?

definitions.note: the word that follows water to make a name for the loo

indicators.note: the losing phrase is placed inside the abbreviation for a court

explanation.surface: Napoleon made no headway in the courts after his defeat at Waterloo.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo suggests the battle Napoleon lost; split as water plus loo, the answer follows water to give water closet, another word for loo.
explanation.definitionFit: A water closet is a flush lavatory, so the word coming after water in that name means loo.

clue.text: Haunt of working bosses

indicators.note: working letters are being put through their paces and rearranged

explanation.surface: A favourite hangout of managers on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: Haunt looks like a noun meaning a regular meeting place; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt someone is to preoccupy their mind persistently, just as to obsess them is.

clue.text: Undeniable rule of good person among poor people

indicators.note: in poor shape the following word is mangled into a new order
being among a crowd puts the good person inside it

explanation.surface: A saintly figure living among the poor follows an indisputable principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor people' reads as one group, but poor only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Estoppel is the legal doctrine barring a party from denying something they previously asserted, so it makes a statement undeniable.

clue.text: Never taken hold of lass because of hair

blocks.note: a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl is grabbed by her hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken hold of' reads as one phrase about seizing; the definition is 'Never taken' and 'hold' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden fortress is a stronghold that has never been captured by an enemy.

clue.text: See 24
Bit of lip from crawler about to desert mad emperor

indicators.note: deserting means leaving, so these letters walk out of the emperor's name

explanation.surface: A grovelling sycophant cheekily abandons an insane ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Crawler suggests a toady giving lip; it is an insect, and the answer is part of its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: In entomology the ligula is the fused tongue-like tip of an insect's labium, its lower mouthpart.

clue.text: Deaths do result from him?

indicators.note: a result is what something works out as, so the preceding letters come out reorganised

explanation.surface: A grim remark on how fatalities follow wherever a certain gunman goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a marksman who never misses leaves fatalities behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead shot is a supremely accurate marksman, so fatalities naturally follow from his shooting.
